source.description:
## PROBLEM

`changelog:check` compares CHANGELOG.md against the generated output for the release range
(previous tag..HEAD). ANY commit landing after the refresh makes the gate red - including a
documentation commit.

Observed on 2026-09-16: the release commit refreshed the changelog and the gate went green; a
127-line session report committed immediately afterwards (docs(report) under .xtrm/reports/, no
source or dist change) turned the gate red on the default branch. Verified rather than inferred:
`bun run changelog:check` -> "CHANGELOG.md: out of date", exit 1, at the post-report HEAD, while
the same command said "already up to date" two commits earlier.

## WHY IT MATTERS

Left unresolved, every post-release documentation or report commit reds the gate on the shared
branch until someone refreshes, which trains readers to ignore a red gate - the same failure mode
as the probe-exit-code trap and the misattributed contract line fixed in this window.

## THE TWO ANSWERS (owner's call, they are not equivalent)

A. ENFORCE REFRESH-LAST: keep the gate as is and treat "refresh the changelog" as the final action
   before a release or tag. The gate keeps meaning "the changelog reflects HEAD". Cost: any later
   commit re-reds it, which is correct but noisy, and it is a process rule that has already been
   broken once by care rather than by haste.

B. EXCLUDE REPORT/DOC INPUTS: if session reports and internal process docs are not user-facing
   release content, exclude that path in the changelog configuration so they do not feed it. The
   gate then stays green after a report lands, at the cost of no longer noticing report commits -
   which is the intent, since they are not changelog material.

Practitioner's note: B is the stabler answer if reports will keep being committed late in a
release window; A is the answer if the changelog is meant to account for every commit. Decide
deliberately rather than by whoever happens to push next.
